synopsis: Nanako drops in on a quiet rehearsal of the public evening and hears a stage line that explains a deliberate blank with the writer's private reason attached. She asks the season's smallest sharp question — is that something to put on stage? The learner trims the line so the gap itself carries the meaning, then decides how Henry keeps his own reason off the public page without the line going cold. The woman who once glossed everything into English so nothing was lost now shows that a chosen omission is authored too, and closes the visit the way she always closes things.

scenes.goal: Reach the point where a rehearsal line that spells out a private reason reads worse on stage than one that stops short and lets the gap carry the meaning.
scenes.dramaticQuestion: Faced with a blank the audience might not understand, will the class explain it all the way down, or trust the omission to speak?
scenes.learnerNeed: A changed-context rewrite where saying less on purpose lands better than saying everything.

nodes.description: The classroom door opens on Henry's phrase 'the truth is.' Nanako stops with her bag still on her shoulder. On the stage script, the next sentence says the earlier writer left town; unlike every other claim on the page, it has no source mark or permission note.

nodes.intent: Arrive as a visitor, apologize lightly for being a little late, and ask only to watch the run-through from the side without stopping it.
nodes.attentionTarget: the taped stage line and the script, seen from the doorway rather than a desk

nodes.intent: Read the draft closing note for the blank route aloud, stacking on the full private reason so the audience will not be confused about why the space was left empty.
nodes.attentionTarget: the printed script line and the imagined audience, more than the people in the room

n2.japanese: じゃあ最後の説明、読むね。『この一区画は、あえて空けてあります。資料をつなぐと、書いた人はその後この街を離れて、続きを書けなかったと考えられます。だから――』……理由までないと、お客さんが迷うかなと思って。

n2.english: Okay, I'll read the closing note. 'This section is left blank on purpose. Taken together, the records suggest that its writer later left town and could not continue. And so—' …I thought the audience might get lost without the reason.

n1.japanese: じゃあ締めの説明、読むよ。『この一区画は、あえて空けてあります。複数の資料をつなぐと、書いた本人はその後この街を離れ、続きを書けなかったと考えられます。ですから――』……理由まで示さないと、なぜ空白なのか、お客さんには伝わらない気がして。

nodes.intent: Gently ask whether the private reason belongs on the stage at all — without correcting him — since the audience can feel the space was deliberate without being told why.
nodes.attentionTarget: the one clause about the writer leaving, and the gap it was meant to explain

n1.english: …Did the person themselves confirm that we may describe on stage the circumstances of leaving town? If not, that clause cannot go in a public script. What we can say ends at 'left blank on purpose.' First, let's read it and stop there.

nodes.resume: The draft line still reads with its full private explanation. The learner steps in to cut it back so the gap itself carries the meaning, keeping only what the audience needs and leaving the writer's reason off the stage.

nodes.resumeContext: The draft closing note reads 「この一区画は、あえて空けてあります。複数の資料をつなぐと、書いた本人はその後この街を離れ、続きを書けなかったと考えられます。ですから――」, but the inferred private circumstance has no publication permission. The learner rewrites it so the deliberate blank still reads as chosen — trimming the private reason and letting an unfinished 〜けど… or a trailing pause do the work — rather than publishing why the writer may have stopped.

nodes.description: Two versions sit side by side on the desk: the full explanation, and a trimmed line that stops at 「あえて空けてあります」 with the rest trailing off. Only the over-explained clause comes back for another pass; the part that already lands stays as it is.

nodes.resume: The closing line now stops short of the private reason. Nanako reads the trimmed version back and names what the gap is doing.

nodes.intent: Read the trimmed line back and name what the omission is doing now: a line chosen and left off the page still counts as writing. This inverts her old habit of glossing everything so nothing was lost.
nodes.attentionTarget: the trailing end of the trimmed line and the silence after it

n2.japanese: うん。じゃあ、舞台の線から読んでみて。……『あえて空けてあります』。そこで三秒。……届いたよ、後ろまで。理由のない説明じゃなくて、許可のある説明になった。

n2.english: Good. Now read it from the stage line. …'Left blank on purpose.' Three seconds there. …It reached the back. This isn't an explanation without a reason; it's an explanation we have leave to give.

n1.japanese: うん。では、舞台の線から読んでみて。……『あえて空けてあります』。そこで三秒。……後ろまで届いたよ。理由を欠いた説明ではなく、許可の範囲で完結した説明になった。
n1.reading: うん。では、ぶたいのせんからよんでみて。……『あえてあけてあります』。そこでさんびょう。……うしろまでとどいたよ。りゆうをかいたせつめいではなく、きょかのはんいでかんけつしたせつめいになった。
n1.english: Good. Now read it from the stage line. …'Left blank on purpose.' Three seconds there. …It reached the back. This isn't an explanation missing its reason; it is a complete explanation within the permission we have.

nodes.description: Henry reads the shorter line from behind the tape and lets the marked three-second pause run. Nanako hears it from the back row without moving closer. The unpermitted clause is covered by a removable strip on the public copy, while the source draft remains intact and face-down.

scenes.goal: Let the learner decide how a contributor's own private reason stays off the public line without the line reading cold, sorting what is private register from what is public.
scenes.dramaticQuestion: Can a stage line keep a reason private and still sound like the person who means it?
scenes.learnerNeed: A stance choice about whether to imply a kept-back reason or leave it fully off the page, holding the private/public register split.

nodes.description: The run-through has stopped at the last page, the line each contributor says in turn. Henry's own line still carries a clause about why the work matters to him, underlined once. In the margin, a small note in his hand reads 「これ要る?」.

nodes.intent: Worry that cutting his own reason will flatten the line into a plain report, so the audience won't feel why the work mattered.
nodes.attentionTarget: his own underlined clause, and how the line sounds stripped of it

n3.japanese: でもここ削ると、なんか…ただの報告みたいにならない?どうしてこれ作ったのか、僕なりの理由もあって。それが無いと、線を説明して終わり、って感じで。

n1.japanese: でも、そこを落とすと、なんだか…ただの報告で終わらない?どうしてこれを作ったのか、僕なりの理由もあるわけで。それを抜くと、地図の説明をして、はい終わり、みたいになりそうで。

nodes.intent: Separate the private reason from the public line — the audience needs to feel the work is real, not to be told why; the reason can stay his, and the line still carries warmth without it.
nodes.attentionTarget: the underlined personal clause, kept for him rather than handed to the room

n2.japanese: その下線、一度、知らない人の前で読めるか考えてみて。少しでも迷うなら、公開版から外そう。『本気で作った』は、声と間で伝わる。理由は、自分用のメモに残せばいい。
n2.reading: そのかせん、いちど、しらないひとのまえでよめるかかんがえてみて。すこしでもまようなら、こうかいばんからはずそう。『ほんきでつくった』は、こえとまでつたわる。りゆうは、じぶんようのメモにのこせばいい。
n2.english: Look at that underlined clause and ask whether you can read it in front of strangers. If you hesitate at all, take it out of the public copy. 'I meant this work' will come through in your voice and the pause. Keep the reason in your own notes.

n1.japanese: その下線を、面識のない人の前でも読めるか、一度考えてみて。わずかでも迷うなら、公開版から外そう。『本気で作った』ことは、声と間で伝えられる。理由そのものは、自分用の注記に残せばいい。
n1.reading: そのかせんを、めんしきのないひとのまえでもよめるか、いちどかんがえてみて。わずかでもまようなら、こうかいばんからはずそう。『ほんきでつくった』ことは、こえとまでつたえられる。りゆうそのものは、じぶんようのちゅうきにのこせばいい。
n1.english: Consider once whether you could read that underlined clause in front of people you have never met. If you hesitate even slightly, remove it from the public copy. Your voice and pause can convey that you meant the work. Keep the reason itself in your private notes.

nodes.question: How should Henry's line handle the reason he wants to keep?

options.action: Keep a trace of it — let the line trail off at "there's a reason, but…" so the audience feels something private without being told it.

japaneseByBand.n3: 「僕には僕の理由があるんですけど……それはここでは。」って、途中で止めよう。あるって分かるだけで十分だよ。
japaneseByBand.n2: 「僕なりの理由もあるんですけど……それはまた。」って、そこで切ろう。理由があるってことだけ、匂わせて渡す。
japaneseByBand.n1: 「僕なりの理由もあるんですけど……それは、また今度。」そこで、ふっと止める。“ある”とだけ伝わればいい――中身は言わずに、気配だけ置いていく。

options.action: Take the reason off the page entirely — let a plain, warm public line stand on its own, and keep the reason only between the people who already know it.

japaneseByBand.n3: 理由は書かないでおこう。「ちゃんと作りました」って、まっすぐだけ言う。知ってる人には、それで伝わるから。
japaneseByBand.n2: 理由の一行は、いっそ全部落とそう。「心を込めて作りました」って、まっすぐだけ残す。知ってる人には、言わなくても届いてるよ。
japaneseByBand.n1: その一行は、いっそ丸ごと下ろしてしまおう。「心を込めて作りました」――それだけ、まっすぐ置く。知っている人には、口にしなくても、もう届いてるものだから。

nodes.resume: The learner has chosen how Henry's line will hold the reason he keeps. Nanako closes the rehearsal the way she always closes things.

nodes.intent: Close cleanly, linking today's chosen omission back to words once left unfinished — some things stay between people on purpose, and that is authorship, not a failure to finish.
nodes.attentionTarget: the trimmed script, and the door she came in by

n2.japanese: うん、今の一回で足りる。全部言わなくても、ちゃんと終われるね。二人の間に残しておくことは、書き忘れじゃない。残すと決めた部分。……私は最終電車があるから、ここまで。じゃあ、当日に。
n2.reading: うん、いまのいっかいでたりる。ぜんぶいわなくても、ちゃんとおわれるね。ふたりのあいだにのこしておくことは、かきわすれじゃない。のこすときめたぶぶん。……わたしはさいしゅうでんしゃがあるから、ここまで。じゃあ、とうじつに。
n2.english: Yes, that one run is enough. We can finish without saying everything. What we choose to leave between two people isn't something we forgot to write. It is the part we chose to keep. …I have a last train, so this is where I stop. See you on the night.

n1.japanese: うん、今の一回で十分。全部を言い切らなくても、きちんと終われるね。二人の間に残すと決めたことは、書き漏らしじゃない。それも書き手の選択だから。……私は最終電車があるので、ここまでにします。じゃあ、当日に。
n1.reading: うん、いまのいっかいでじゅうぶん。ぜんぶをいいきらなくても、きちんとおわれるね。ふたりのあいだにのこすときめたことは、かきもらしじゃない。それもかきてのせんたくだから。……わたしはさいしゅうでんしゃがあるので、ここまでにします。じゃあ、とうじつに。
n1.english: Yes, that one run is enough. We can finish cleanly without saying everything. What we decide to leave between two people isn't an omission by mistake. That, too, is an author's choice. …I have a last train, so I'll stop here. See you on the night.

nodes.intent: Accept the cut without arguing it back, keeping only what he can hand to everyone and letting the rest stay his — the tool-first talker leaving a line understandable without over-explaining it.
nodes.attentionTarget: the shortened line, and the fact that it still sounds like him

n2.reading: ……りょうかい。『ぶたいよう』と『じぶんようのちゅうき』。いま、べつファイルにする。きづいてくれて、ありがとう。

nodes.description: Two filenames appear on Henry's screen: STAGE and PRIVATE NOTES. The public line keeps its three-second pause; the personal clause remains untouched in the private copy. Nanako checks the train time, lifts one hand from the doorway, and is gone before Henry can reopen either file.

callbacks.meaningNow: Nanako's habit of glossing everything into English so no one is stranded inverts into its payoff: she shows that a line chosen and left off the page is authored meaning, and that a private reason can stay off the public register without the line going cold.
callbacks.optionalFallback: Nanako, visiting the rehearsal, simply helps trim a stage line so a deliberate blank and a kept-back reason carry the meaning, without any callback to her earlier glossing habit.

outcomes.description: The rehearsal script's closing lines are trimmed so a deliberate blank reads as chosen and a contributor's private reason is kept off the public page, while the line still reads as the person's own; the public evening's script now carries meaning in what it leaves unsaid.

Nanako returns as a visitor and, instead of glossing everything so nothing is lost, teaches the class that a chosen omission is authored; her Arrival habit of leaving no one stranded inverts into deliberate leaving-unsaid, and the class can now ask her judgment on what stays private.
